newsitem.title: UK: Land Securities up as results top forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Land Securities up as results top forecasts.

text.p: Shares in property group Land Securities Plc were marked sharply higher in pre-market trade on Wednesday after the property company posted better-than-expected profits for the year ended March 31.
The stock was up 20-1/2p at 864-1/2 by 0707 GMT in volume of 235,000 shares, dragging up other property stocks.
British Land Plc was up 13p at 573-1/2, Brixton Estates Plc was up 4p at 202-1/2, MEPC Plc was up 7-1/2p at 493-1/2 and Hammerson Plc was up 5-1/2p at 453.
Interest-rate sensitive property stocks were also boosted by overnight news that the U.S. Federal Reserve had left short-term rates unchanged at a key monetary policy meeting.
Land Securities posted a rise in pre-tax profit to 243.8 million stg from 237 million a year before, compared with analyst forecasts mostly in a range between 230 million stg and 240 million.
The company also reported a better-than-expected 13 percent rise in its net asset value per share to 783p.

"The profits were obviously at the very top end of expectations but the net asset value is the big thing," said one dealer, "on this basis you would have to say that the whole sector could be re-rated and that is what's exciting people."

Land Securities said the the future was "somewhat uncertain" after the Labour party's recent election victory but it was hoping that new policies would "create sufficient confidence to add further stimulus to the property market".
"We look forward with greater confidence as income flows from our developments and as the portfolio benefits from the rental growth we are now seeing in the market," the company said.
By 0807 GMT Land Securities shares were up 33p at 877, while British Land -- its partner in the FTSE 100 index of blue chip stocks -- was up 16p at 576-1/2.
